correctness.rationale: The median map is continuous and piecewise linear with finite selector matrices; each matrix has exactly one 1 per row, and its ell_p operator norm is max column multiplicity raised to 1/p. All global maxima occur in some strict-order chamber and are attained as a two-input local perturbation. For fixed pivotal site zero, simultaneous balance of m windows is equivalent to k residue-class chain equalities. Chain intersection sizes are exactly q or q+1, giving a necessary-and-sufficient subset-sum condition. The n=m+1 exact count and explicit (n,r)=(10,3) six-row witness were checked algebraically. The checker passes 60 exhaustive bounded cases and 100 arithmetic family checks, but finite tests are not the universal proof.

value.rationale: Finite cyclic median filtering is a standard nonlinear smoother, and simultaneous perturbation of overlapping windows has an a priori m-fold ell_p amplification bound. The theorem gives a complete arithmetic classification across all cycle lengths, windows and finite p of precisely when that bound is attainable; odd cycles always attain it, certain even cycles do not, and the shortest nontrivial even cycle has exact amplification only (r+1)^(1/p). This structural parity/arithmetic law is a motivated robustness boundary, not a single arbitrary parameter enumeration. It does not require a paper-sized general all-subcritical-norm theorem.
